title: a sieve's seal covers the folder it declares it scans
intention: A proof whose subject is a folder declares SCANS, a list of repo-relative globs. Its seal's fingerprint covers what those globs match, so a repair to a scanned file, or a new matching file, moves the fingerprint and the commit's reseal re-runs the sieve instead of keeping its red as settled.
why: Measured 2026-11-20 on akiendelllinux: the build commits for 0dbb6b5e940a (8ab52a07a) and f92d213f7dd0 (b47a845c1) each repaired files that two tester sieves scan. Both reseals printed those sieves as 'RED ... (rung 1 — settled ...)' even though diagnostic runs read them green twice. A sieve's closure holds the code it executes, never the files it reads, so the repair could not move its fingerprint, and only re-running it by name cleared it.
traces_to: Law 1 (a settled answer is not re-derived, so the fingerprint must say what the answer was taken over) and Law 8 (a seal must measure its subject).
how: The tester's seal reads a proof's module-level SCANS by ast.literal_eval (never by import), records evidence.scans, and unions the matches into fingerprint_closure. validation_store.closure_of, the one reader of a seal's closure, re-expands evidence.scans on each read. The two tester sieves declare SCANS. A red-first proof seals a fixture sieve and reads the fingerprint move.

clauses.claim: a fixture sieve proof declaring SCANS, sealed through the tester, records evidence.scans and a fingerprint_closure naming every file its globs match
after editing a file the SCANS globs match, sealed_fingerprint_now differs from the seal's recorded source_fingerprint
after adding a new file the SCANS globs match, sealed_fingerprint_now differs from the seal's recorded source_fingerprint
reseal with skip_settled over a sieve sealed red whose scanned file has since changed runs the proof, and does not return outcome settled-red

constraints: b7d5df9919fe clause 3 holds: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_module_loaded_by_path_is_in_the_seals_closure.py stays green, and a file a proof only reads as data, undeclared, stays out of its closure
a proof without SCANS seals the same fingerprint_closure as before the build

the two tester sieves cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_tester_proofs_measure_only_tester.py and cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_testers_proofs_reach_temp_only_through_the_scratch_door.py keep every tooth's assertion and stay green

decisions.text: D1: validation_store.closure_of unions the sorted, repo-relative matches of evidence.scans (globs rooted at _REPO_ROOT, files only) into the recorded closure when evidence.scans is a list; it returns None exactly where it does today.

D2: at the seal (device.py near _read_closure's call), the tester reads the proof's module-level SCANS with ast.literal_eval, records evidence['scans'], and joins its matches to the closure; a glob that matches nothing, or reaches outside the repo, is named in the run's output and not recorded.

D3: the scratch-door sieve declares SCANS for the proofs it rglobs (cairn/devices/tester/**/proofs/test_*.py); measure_only_tester declares the tester tree it hands encapsulation_breaches (cairn/devices/tester/**/*.py).

D4: the red-first proof builds its fixture sieve under scratch_dir, one tooth per clause, and checks constraint 1 by running cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_module_loaded_by_path_is_in_the_seals_closure.py.

out: every other component; reseal.py is read, not written

measured.saw: both build-commit reseals printed 'reseal: N resealed · 3 settled-red' and named the two tester sieves as settled red, while bin/cairn test read each sieve green on two diagnostic passes (tester runs test-96f4befd5416, test-2098cdca851a, test-9844e5f56b23, test-e31e27f66b35)

reseal.py:740 skips a red seal when sealed_fingerprint_now equals the recorded source_fingerprint; device.py:894 takes the closure from executed files plus the reach log only; closure_of (validation_store.py:339) is read at validation_store.py:364 and :609 and reseal.py:687 and :1114
measured.how: grep and sed of the house tree at 60c0cf4f5 on akiendelllinux
